message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.34","text":"Oh, the great hand of the wise God, which makes all things in all things! For a countless multitude of birds has been brought into being by him, and this multitude is diverse, each bird differing from another in every respect—I mean their colors, beaks, claws, eyes, dispositions, voices, and all the other features. And how many different forms of plants there are, distinguished by countless colors, qualities, and scents! How many animals of the dry land and how many of those in the waters, whose shapes, forms, locations, colors, ways of life, dispositions, natures, and multitude it is impossible to tell! There are also the numbers and heights of mountains, the differences among stones, fearsome recesses, springs, rivers, lakes, seas, harbors, islands, forests, the whole inhabited world, and uninhabited places.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς μεγάλης θεοῦ φρονίμου χειρός","chosen":"the great hand of the wise God","rationale":"The masculine genitive φρονίμου agrees with θεοῦ, describing God as wise, while μεγάλης agrees with χειρός and describes the hand as great."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐν πᾶσιν πάντα ποιούσης","chosen":"which makes all things in all things","rationale":"The rendering preserves the repeated πᾶς wording and its broad scope. “Which does everything in every sphere” is a possible interpretive alternative."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὗτος ποικίλος, πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κατὰ πάντα ἐξηλλαγμένος","chosen":"and this multitude is diverse, each bird differing from another in every respect","rationale":"The collective noun ὄχλος is masculine singular, and οὗτος and ἐξηλλαγμένος agree with it grammatically. The main rendering understands the comparison distributively among the birds because the following catalogue names their distinguishing features. Alternatively, the phrase may compare one collective group or kind of birds with another: “and this multitude is diverse, differing in every respect from the other [group or kind].”"},{"source_quote":"βλέμματα, γνώμας, φθέγματα","chosen":"eyes, dispositions, voices","rationale":"βλέμματα can mean looks, gazes, or eyes; γνώμαι denotes dispositions or traits of mind; φθέγματα denotes uttered sounds or voices."},{"source_quote":"θέσεις","chosen":"locations","rationale":"θέσις literally denotes placement or position. In this catalogue of animal differences, “locations” is cautious; “habitats” or “postures” are possible contextual alternatives."},{"source_quote":"ὀρέων πλήθη καὶ ὕψη","chosen":"the numbers and heights of mountains","rationale":"The plural πλήθη denotes the quantity or numerousness of the mountains; “multitudes and heights of mountains” is a more formally corresponding alternative."},{"source_quote":"μυχοὺς φοβερούς","chosen":"fearsome recesses","rationale":"μυχός denotes an inner recess or depth. “Fearsome depths” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὕλας","chosen":"forests","rationale":"Although ὕλη can mean matter or material, the geographical catalogue supports its concrete sense “woods” or “forests.”"}],"source_issues":[]}]}
